hints.title: Paid versus Free Painter Resource Allocation Obstacle
hints.text: The paid painter paints one wall in time[i] units at cost[i]. During that time, the free painter can paint time[i] additional walls for free. How can choosing walls for the paid painter ensure all n walls are painted for minimum total cost?

hints.title: Wall Coverage Weight Equivalence Invariant
hints.text: Each wall painted by the paid painter yields 1 + time[i] total walls painted (itself plus free painter walls). The goal is finding the minimum cost to acquire at least n wall units.

hints.title: 1D Array Knapsack Capacity Cap Procedure
hints.text: Initialize an array of size n + 1 with infinity, setting entry 0 to 0. For each wall i, let gain = 1 + time[i]. Iterate backward from n down to 0: update entry j to min(entry j, cost[i] + entry max(0, j - gain)). Return entry n.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Iterates through N walls, updating 1D array of size N + 1 backwards.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating 2^N wall assignment combinations causes timeout.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Compresses state space into 1D buffer of length N + 1.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Reframing the problem as 0/1 knapsack where items have weight 1 + time[i] and cost cost[i].
